meta.name: Motif to APQC-Process Crosswalk
meta.purpose: Marries the 12 neural control motifs (LIMEN Neural-to-Business Motif Crosswalk) to the APQC Process Classification Framework (cross-industry, the universal taxonomy of what firms DO). This is the STRUCTURAL layer: motif -> business FUNCTION/PROCESS, falsifiable by failure-mode match. It deliberately stops at function. The node->company (specific-firm) layer is empirical and out of scope here by design.
meta.stance: Built affirmatively. Each mapping is constructed, evidenced against process mechanism, and tiered by isomorphism strength. Refutation-by-expert (treating a domain professional as the held-out validation set) is the crosswalk doc's OWN next step and is NOT applied here; you cannot refute a mapping before it is built.
sources: LIMEN Neural to Business Motif Crosswalk (Jul 8 2026)
APQC Process Classification Framework, cross-industry (13 categories, 1,000+ processes)
SOC 2018 / O*NET (occupation-level task and work-context detail used as mechanism evidence)

apqc_categories.name: Develop and Manage Products and Services
Market and Sell Products and Services
Manage Enterprise Risk, Compliance, Remediation, and Resiliency

tiers.STRONG: Mechanism-matched on both sides and both failure poles rhyme; the process IS the control primitive, not merely adjacent to it.
tiers.MODERATE-STRONG: Mechanism matches and failure poles rhyme, but the process spans two horizons or is thinner than a full standing function.
tiers.MODERATE: A real and common analogy; hold to the mechanism, not the vibe. Verify per instance before relying on it.
tiers.PARAMETER: Maps a balance parameter, not a standalone process/entity; apply it to how tightly any unit self-limits.

precision_family_note: Motifs 2, 5, and 6 (gain, switching, prediction-error) are the same operation at different resolutions: weighting representations by estimated reliability. Motifs 1 and 8 are precision applied as suppression. The failure modes rhyme because they are all versions of the weighting being wrong: too much trust in the model (M6 priors-too-strong, M1 over-grip) or too little (fragmentation, brake-failure).

motifs.name: Top-down inhibitory brake
motifs.control_primitive: A higher control node suppresses a faster, reactive lower unit (negative-sign, top-down edge).
motifs.brain: vmPFC -> BLA/CeA (extinction, cited); vlPFC -> amygdala (reappraisal); PFC -> subcortical generally.
motifs.business_function: Oversight that suppresses a reactive revenue unit via a slower top-down signal: risk/compliance overriding a trading desk; legal holding back sales; an editor gating a newsroom.
motifs.failure_over: Over-grip: the brake strangles the unit (compliance kills all risk-taking).
motifs.failure_under: Brake-failure: the reactive unit runs unchecked (rogue desk, fraud).
motifs.validation_test: Does the function actually INHIBIT a reactive unit via a slower top-down signal, or merely sit 'above' it on an org chart? Only the former matches.

motifs.name: Gain / broadcast modulation
motifs.control_primitive: One small node sets system-wide gain or threshold, one-to-many, multiplicative.
motifs.brain: LC -> cortex (norepinephrine, arousal/precision); RAPHE (5-HT); VTA (DA); NBM (ACh).

processes: Set cost of capital / hurdle rate

motifs.business_function: A single signal that rescales everyone's behavior at once: a central-bank rate (the LC of an economy), a firm-wide alert level, a firm-wide incentive multiplier or hurdle rate.
motifs.failure_over: Gain stuck high: hypervigilance, everything reads as urgent, resources thrash (panic markets).
motifs.failure_under: Gain stuck low: signals missed, sluggish response (complacency before a crash).
motifs.validation_test: Does the candidate set a GLOBAL multiplier on many units simultaneously, or act on one channel? Broadcast != point-to-point.

motifs.name: Homeostatic negative feedback
motifs.control_primitive: Output feeds back to shut off its own trigger, usually delayed.
motifs.brain: HPA cortisol -> HIPP/HYPO/PIT; autoreceptors (D2, a2, 5-HT1A); baroreflex.
motifs.business_function: Self-correcting loops: audit/governance cycles, budget-to-actual variance correction, inventory-reorder loops, automatic stabilizers.
motifs.failure_over: Feedback too aggressive/delayed: oscillation (bullwhip effect, credit cycling).
motifs.failure_under: Feedback broken: runaway (asset bubble, unchecked cost spiral).
motifs.validation_test: Trace the loop: does the output measurably SUPPRESS its own cause after a lag? If there is no closing arrow, it is not this motif.

motifs.name: Gating relay (adjustable throughput)
motifs.control_primitive: A hub passes or blocks signal based on system state.
motifs.brain: THAL (+TRN self-inhibition); basal-ganglia gate STRI -> GP -> THAL; SC.
motifs.business_function: Throughput gates: procurement/approval workflows, capital-release gates, credit-approval committees, a CFO releasing or holding spend.
motifs.failure_over: Gate stuck open: flooding, no filtering (uncontrolled spend).
motifs.failure_under: Gate stuck closed: starvation, bottleneck (frozen capital, project starvation).
motifs.validation_test: Is throughput STATE-DEPENDENT and adjustable, or fixed? A gate modulates; a pipe does not.

motifs.name: Switching / resource reallocation
motifs.control_primitive: An arbiter shifts control between mutually-exclusive competing modes.
motifs.business_function: Attention/capital reallocation between business-as-usual and crisis; a portfolio rotating defensive <-> growth; an exec team pivoting the org.
motifs.failure_over: Thrashing: switches too fast, no mode completes (strategy whiplash).
motifs.failure_under: Stuck in one mode: cannot switch to respond (rigid org misses a market shift).
motifs.validation_test: Does the candidate DETECT salience and REALLOCATE between competing systems, or just run one system well? Switching requires an arbiter above both modes.

motifs.name: Feedforward prediction + error correction
motifs.control_primitive: A model predicts; mismatch (error) propagates and updates the model.
motifs.brain: Predictive coding V1 feedback/feedforward (cited); cerebellar climbing-fiber error.
motifs.business_function: Forecasting + variance analysis: budget-vs-actual driving correction, demand forecasting, actuarial pricing/reserving, planning cycles that update on surprise.
motifs.failure_over: Priors too strong: ignores disconfirming data (plans from belief not data).
motifs.failure_under: No stable model: over-reacts to every fluctuation (noise-chasing, fragmentation).
motifs.validation_test: Does the candidate maintain an EXPLICIT predictive model that gets updated by error, or just react? Prediction-error minimization is the signature.

motifs.name: Sustained vs phasic threat monitoring
motifs.control_primitive: Tonic (sustained, uncertain) vs phasic (acute, specific) alarm on the same channel, two timescales.
motifs.business_function: Continuous risk-monitoring / early-warning systems (tonic) vs incident response (phasic): the same channel harvestable at two horizons. This is the ladder/arc horizon-orthogonality made concrete.
motifs.failure_over: Tonic stuck on: chronic alarm, burnout, resource drain (permanent crisis footing).
motifs.failure_under: Phasic hair-trigger: overreaction to non-threats (false-alarm incident spam).
motifs.validation_test: Distinguish the two timescales: is the function sustained-vigilance or acute-response? Mapping both to one channel is the tonic/phasic distinction, not a duplicate.

motifs.name: Anti-reward brake (KILLSWITCH)
motifs.control_primitive: Inhibitory suppression of the reward/motivation channel itself.
motifs.business_function: The brake on reward-seeking: drawdown limits, stop-losses, a strategy kill switch, a committee that cuts a beloved-but-losing project. This is literally the KILLSWITCH structure.
motifs.failure_over: Anti-reward too strong: anhedonia, nothing worth pursuing (no risk appetite, paralysis).
motifs.failure_under: Too weak: chases losses, cannot quit (sunk-cost escalation).
motifs.validation_test: Does the candidate SUPPRESS pursuit of a reward on a negative signal, or just fail to reward? Active anti-reward != absence of reward.
motifs.note: Often NOT a standing named process but a structure invoked on a negative signal. Absence of a clean APQC standing process is itself a finding, not a failure of the mapping.

motifs.name: Local E/I balance (unit self-regulation)
motifs.control_primitive: Local feedback inhibition keeps a unit stable (this is the E/I parameter, not a node).
motifs.brain: GABAergic PV/SST interneuron feedback throughout cortex.

processes: Manage internal controls within a unit

motifs.business_function: Internal controls WITHIN a unit: a team's own QA, local budget discipline, self-limiting processes that keep a unit from running away on its own.
motifs.failure_over: Too much inhibition: the unit cannot act (over-controlled paralysis, process strangulation).
motifs.failure_under: Too little inhibition: the unit destabilizes (seizure-like runaway, over-extension).
motifs.validation_test: This maps a PARAMETER, not an entity. Apply it to how tightly any unit self-limits, not to a standalone firm/function.

motifs.name: Interoceptive aggregation -> salience
motifs.control_primitive: Afferent internal-state signals aggregate and get salience-weighted.
motifs.business_function: Internal telemetry: KPI dashboards, ops-metrics aggregation, the system that decides WHICH internal signal is worth escalating.
motifs.failure_over: Over-weighted: every internal fluctuation escalates (metric obsession).
motifs.failure_under: Poor interoception: the system cannot feel its own state (flying blind, no consolidated view).
motifs.validation_test: Does it AGGREGATE internal signals and assign salience, or report externally? Interoception is inward-sensing.

motifs.name: Reward / motivation drive
motifs.control_primitive: Value-weighted drive channels resources toward expected return.
motifs.business_function: Incentive structures, compensation design, capital flowing toward expected return.
motifs.failure_over: Drive too high: over-pursuit, bubbles (mania, addiction).
motifs.validation_test: Does it weight action by EXPECTED VALUE and drive pursuit? Many things 'motivate'; this one assigns incentive salience.

motifs.name: Rhythm generation / entrainment
motifs.control_primitive: A pacemaker sets cadence; units entrain to it.
motifs.business_function: Operational cadence: reporting cycles, sprint rhythms, market open/close, settlement cycles, synchronization across teams.
motifs.failure_over: Over-rigid rhythm: cannot adapt timing to events (bureaucratic cadence ignoring reality).
motifs.failure_under: Desynchronization: units out of phase, coordination collapse (misaligned teams).
motifs.validation_test: Is there a PACEMAKER others entrain to, or just a schedule? Entrainment requires phase-locking to a source.
